# The Fruit as Plant Advertising

Fruit is a plant's advertising medium to ensure the dispersal of its seeds. How does this happen? Why do tomatoes turn red when they're ready to eat? Why is it not advisable to eat a potato that has turned green? And what should you do if garlic cloves turn blue? Many plants have a dialogue with the animals that eat them, not in spoken language but in shapes and colors designed to catch the eye and stimulate our hunger. To understand how plants speak to us, it's first important to understand what they gain from the deal. When an animal eats a fruit, it takes the fruit's seeds for a ride and "leaves" them somewhere else inside a pile of manure—an excellent starting point for a new plant to sprout. Thus, a plant that succeeded in producing better and more attractive fruits for animals spread faster and over time also traveled farther.

The critical part of the agreement is that the fruit must signal when it's ready for the ride: a tomato, for example, is green and bitter before it's ready. The green color is chlorophyll, just like in leaves. The bitter taste is caused by substances designed to persuade us not to eat the fruit until the right moment. What is the right moment? When the fruit's seed has finished developing and is ready for its short journey through the digestive system. A ripe fruit is essentially an advertisement—it's larger and has a sweeter taste than an unripe fruit, becomes softer, and also releases a scent that attracts animals.

## How Do Fruits Ripen?

Most fruits ripen in response to the plant hormone ethylene. This is a small molecule carried through the air, which is why to speed up the ripening of avocados or bananas, you should put them in a bag with another ripe fruit. Apples are usually picked before they're ripe and stored in a cooled environment with a high percentage of air filtration and carbon dioxide to prevent them from absorbing the ethylene they themselves emit. This way, you can extend their shelf life by months. Sometimes you see an apple that looks as though only half of it has ripened, and in most cases the reason will be partial exposure to ethylene during the ripening process. Not all plants allow you to do this trick, though—wild berries, for example, must ripen on the branch, and if you pick them too early, they'll rot without ripening.

The ripening process begins in the fruit's inner tissue when the seed signals that it's approaching readiness. This way, the seed and the entire fruit ripen together. The fruit becomes sweeter by producing sugars, loses its bitter taste, and softens. In the fruit's skin, the green chlorophyll breaks down, and simultaneously, the plant produces pigments designed to protect the fruit and also give it a more striking hue. These pigments fall into two large groups: carotenoids and anthocyanins, and both groups have striking colors and antioxidant properties that apparently protect the fruit.

Carotenoids are responsible for the red, orange, and yellow colors you can see, for example, in tomatoes and carrots. Carotenoids also give many animals their characteristic color, such as the pink of salmon and flamingos. These animals don't produce carotenoids; they obtain them from their food.

Anthocyanins are responsible for the red, purple, and blue colors you can see in plants like raspberries, blueberries, black beans, and red cabbage. With red cabbage, you can do a home experiment that demonstrates the following phenomenon: the color of anthocyanins depends on the acidity level (pH) of their environment. Anthocyanins are water-soluble, so you can prepare a solution of dye from red cabbage and test the acidity of substances by the color changes they cause in the solution.

## Other Colors, Other Reasons

Even non-fruit parts may change color. Garlic cloves change color in response to changes in acidity, but not because of the presence of anthocyanins. Garlic contains the molecule alliin, which under high acidity conditions or heating reacts with amino acids to form cyclic molecules—that is, compounds made up of rings of carbon and additional atoms. In this specific molecule, two rings will produce a red color, three rings a blue color, and four rings a green color like chlorophyll (which also has four similar rings). All are edible, and in China, colored garlic cloves are considered festive. Blue pickled garlic is used in China to celebrate the Laba Festival.

A potato, for example, turns green and can become unfit for consumption, but this is not a ripening process. Potato tubers are not fruit but rather part of the stem that burrows underground and accumulates starch. Therefore, potatoes have no strong smell or striking color and are hidden from view. Their role for the plant is to serve as an energy storage or to sprout more potato plants in a process called vegetative reproduction (like runners). Despite its resemblance to a sweet potato, the potato plant is a relative of the tomato and also has fruit, although they're not suitable for eating. Most tissues of the plant contain a poison called solanine. Potatoes that have begun to sprout start to produce chlorophyll, which makes them turn green, and solanine, which makes them toxic.

Besides colors, there are many other signs that plants use to communicate, both with animals and with each other—but that's a story for another time.

## What Happens to Fruit When the Tree Is Thirsty

So then, what is the nutritional weight of the color of a green or red fruit in relation to the nutritional weight of the rest of the vegetable or fruit?

What's the reason? To produce the purple betalain in beets or the orange carotene in carrots, both plants use chemical reactions between different substances. To use our example, a person who eats only carrots could develop nutritional deficiencies in substances that aren't in carrots but are in beets (vitamins, minerals, etc.). On the other hand, in the supermarket there are tons of tomatoes in many colors, and apart from differences in the level of lycopene (an antioxidant; we wrote about it once here), their biology is very similar and they will usually contain similar amounts of the same vitamins, minerals, etc.

**Regarding the second part of your question:** In terms of quantity, the molecule that gives the plant its color is a very small percentage of the molecules that make up the plant, but every substance has a different nutritional value. Let's take a carrot as an example. A carrot is orange because of a high percentage of molecules called carotenoids, among which is beta-carotene, which the human body uses to produce vitamin A, which is essential for vision, the immune system, and other body functions. The other substances in the carrot are also necessary for the human body in varying amounts, and therefore it's mainly good to think about diversity in the vegetables and fruits we eat. The diversity of colors is useful to us to generally know which vitamins and minerals we can get from each plant. By the way, vitamins and plants were also written about here! It's recommended to read if you're interested. A common rule of thumb is that you should eat vegetables in 5 different colors every day. Why is this a good rule of thumb? To my understanding, because it ensures that we eat at least 5 vegetables a day and that they will be relatively diverse.

There is also criticism of the way gossip can be spread and compensated for without consequences on social networks.

מה עיוותתי"), אלינה מחליטה להמשיך את הרומן הסוחף שלהם ולוקחת אותו לסיבוב בעוד משימה. על רקע ריאיון שהתפרסם לאחרונה עם שורד העבר עומר רוזן, שדיבר על כך שמתמודדים שההפקה הייתה חפצה ביקרם, קיבלו משימות חסינות שנראות כאילו הן תפורות למידותיהם, קשה שלא לתהות אם גם המשימה הזאת לכל הפחות נוחה לאלינה, הרקדנית בעלת היציבה החזקה. שלא במפתיע, היא מנצחת ולוקחת את קולו של רגב, מה שמביא למהפך בקולות וכעת הברית של עידן וירדן היא זאת שמובילה. לאכול את העוגה ולהשאיר אותה שלמה הפרק של מוצ"ש נפתח בווידוי העצוב של אלה, על כך שהתקשתה לייצר קשרים משמעותיים עם בנות לאורך חייה, ואנחנו מבטיחים שאם לא יצא לה משפט לא נחמד כלפי מישהו בפרקים הבאים, אנחנו עוד עשויים להתחיל לחבב אותה. אבל עזבו - המנה העיקרית בפרק הזה היא משימת המכירה הפומבית, שתמיד כיף לראות. רגע לפני - הדירוג החברתי שלא ממש רלוונטי לאיש, מלבד המדורג במקום האחרון. במקרה הזה מדובר כצפוי בבני, שנשללת ממנו הזכות להשתתף. פייר, אין מבאס מזה. לא נזכיר את כל החבילות, אבל הנה כמה רגעים שאהבנו במיוחד: הרגע הכי נחמד: "כרטיס השחקן" שקנה עידן חביב ומאפשר לו להכניס את בני למשחק בכל זאת או לקבל סכום כסף נוסף עבור עצמו. עידן בוחר כמובן בצעד חברי/אסטרטגי נבון לצרף את בני למשחק. אמנם ישראל מיהר לעקוץ בטסטה על כך שהכל אסטרטגיה בשרשרת החיול, ושעידן לא באמת אוהב את בני, אבל היי - מיד אחר כך קארמה סידרה לעידן מנת סביח. יש צדק בעולם. הרגע הכי מצחיק: במקרה הזה מדובר בכל אחת מהרכישות של רגב, שקיבל שוב ושוב מגיא את ההזדמנות להחליף את החבילה שבחר באחת אחרת, ושוב ושוב נשאר עם החבילות שבחר, עד לרגע בו הורם הקלוש והוא גילה לתדהמתו פריטים "חיוניים" כמו מזרק בוטוקס וקיסם שיניים. ואנחנו חשבנו שבני הוא הדמות הקומית של העונה. • להיטי קיץ 2020: מנותקים, נמאסתם • השחקנית שרצתה לעזוב את "חברים" הרגע הבאמת הכי-מצחיק: אבל עם כל הכבוד לפדיחות של רגב, אלה נפלה בגדול בפח של גיא כשהכריז על חבילה שגורמת לו לעשות תנועות סיבוביות. וזה עוד אחרי שזכתה בחבילה המועילה של "איפור-שיער", כן? # Survivor: Everyone Against Everyone

The public auction arrived just in time to show us that from now on it's every survivor for themselves • Coming soon: our bets on the finale • Episodes 44-45 on Matcha

Friends, we're excited to announce - the finale is around the corner. Of course, by "around the corner" we mean you still need to travel dozens more hours through an endless stream of mind-numbing events, take a turn at the "Villa of the Eliminated," stop at "Big Disputes Square," and get stuck at dozens of special traffic lights on the way to the finale. In short, despite there already being an estimated date, there's still a long way to go, and during which, judging by the promo, the survivors will manage to switch alliances like socks. We're in any case starting to bet on who makes it to the finale, but we'll save that for a separate column, if you don't mind.

## A New Era

In Tuesday's episode, the survivors are also starting to smell the finale - Assi is displaying an outward demeanor of calm, but internally he's already divvying up the jury votes. It's not good for him to reach the finale with his allies, since they're actually the ones who could vote for him as jurors, while continuing his competition with them will be a struggle for jury votes already eliminated. They ate from the same trough and that's it.

Assi made a clever and rather surprising move and turned to form an alliance with Eden. The fact that he initiated it perhaps makes him more "dirty," but it's a strategically brilliant move and Eden the tycoon understands this too and was happy to cooperate. This is double risk, because beyond the fact that they need to eliminate their friends delicately so the jurors don't turn against them, they're now dependent on each other's mercy. Assi didn't hesitate to betray his friends in the past, and Eden might still surprise.

In the negotiation hut, Alina befriends herself with her feelings, and gives us another gaping mouth, discovering that she needs to eat a huge bowl of peanut butter to beat Ragev. On the agenda - a conversation with Rafael Chavibi (father of), who understands that Alina's staying will help Eden more and decides to encourage her specifically. Ragev also doesn't seem eager to win the challenge, and Alina scores a first and significant victory.

## Survivor: Island Wretches

## Survivor: What If?

But does the alliance situation get shaken up again like a sponge? Because here Jordan turns to Assi and offers him... wait, what did she offer him? It was something like "I won't leave my alliance and you won't leave yours, but I enjoy watching you play and maybe we'll do something." We didn't understand - do you want to exercise together? Sign up for a macramé class? Join "Bozglos"? Bottom line, Jordan wanted to go and feel free, and Assi gently waved her off, just like a Tinder chat where it's clear it's going nowhere and the other side says "we'll talk tomorrow," really meaning "let's pretend this never happened."

Let's jump ahead to the next duel challenge, which Alina entered skipping. Pier - despite barely seeing her five minutes - we missed her. After Ragev gets irritated for a moment over the word "twisted" ("Why twisted? What did I twist?"), Alina decides to continue their riveting romance and takes him on another challenge. Against the backdrop of a recently published interview with past survivor Omer Rozen, who spoke about how the production wanted competitors' praise, received immunity challenges that seem tailored to their measurements, it's hard not to wonder if this challenge too is at least comfortable for Alina, the dancer with strong stability. Unsurprisingly, she wins and takes Ragev's vote, causing a flip in votes and now Eden and Jordan's alliance is leading.

## Eating the Cake and Keeping It Whole

Saturday's episode opens with Ella's sad confession about struggling to form meaningful connections with girls throughout her life, and we promise if she didn't get a nasty sentence toward someone in the coming episodes, we might start liking her. But never mind - the main course in this episode is the public auction challenge, which is always fun to watch.

A moment before - the social ranking that's not really relevant to anyone except the one ranked last. In this case it's as expected Beni, who was denied participation. Pier, there's nothing worse than that.

We won't mention all the packages, but here are some moments we especially loved:

**The nicest moment:** The "player card" that Eden Chavibi bought, allowing him to either bring Beni into the game or get extra money for himself. Eden of course chooses the friendly/smart strategic move to include Beni in the game. While Israel was quick to bite at the fact that it's all strategy in the food chain, and that Eden doesn't really love Beni, hey - immediately after that karma gave Eden a slap. There's justice in the world.

**The funniest moment:** In this case it's every single one of Ragev's purchases, where Gia kept giving him the chance to swap the package he chose for another, and he kept staying with his choices, until the moment when the weak one lifted and he discovered "essential" items like Botox injections and dental floss. And we thought Beni was the comic character of the season.

**The most-actually-funniest moment:** But with all due respect to Ragev's blunders, Ella fell big into Gia's trap when he announced a package that makes him do rotational movements. And this after she won the useful "makeup-hair" package, right? She sent 650 pesos toward Gia and squealed toward him in joy, but when the weak one was lifted it turned out to be a picture of hummus and not the real thing. "How could you do this to me?" she blurted out in offense, and after the sense of discomfort passed over us, we had to be lifted off the floor from laughing.

**The most delicious moment:** Jordan waited and waited and at some point it became annoying - where's your sportsmanship? But like in competitions against a tough female judoka from a foreign country, Jordan knew exactly what she was doing. ויחידות עילית בצה"ל. היחידה היא מקור הסמכה וידע למבצעים מורכבים.  היסטוריה ופעילות מבצעית הקמה במהלך שנת 1977 פעל מתקן 5135 ברפיח להכשרת נהגי סיור אוגדתיים. בשנת 1979, בעקבות הסכם השלום בין ישראל למצרים, המתקן עבר לצאלים. בשנת 1980 הוקם "בית ספר למודיעין וסיור" (מו"ס), לאימוני יחידות מודיעין וסיור. בשנת 1996 הוקם מדור נהיגה מבצעית במו"ס. בשנת 1999, בעקבות תאונה של פלס"ר 500, התבצע לראשונה קורס נהיגה מבצעית. בשנת 2001 הוקם בית ספר למודיעין שדה, (ביסלמ"ש) יחידת הנהיגה המבצעית נשארה כחלק מביסלמ"ש בצאלים. בשנת 2004, בעקבות תאונה בתרגיל של גדוד 71, התקבלה החלטה בזרוע היבשה להקים את בית הספר לניוד מבצעי. יישום ההחלטה התבצע בשנת 2005, עם הקמתו של בית הספר. בשנת 2010, לאחר עבודת מטה ממושכת, התרחב בית הספר למתכונתו הנוכחית. עם הזמן ייעודה האופרטיבי של היחידה התחדד והתגבש לביצוע משימות ניוד מבצעי מיוחד בשגרה ובחירום, באמצעות כלי רכב גלגליים בחזית ובעומק החזית. כפועל יוצא מן היכולות המבצעיות בתחום הניוד מופעלת היחידה במצב חירום וכפופה לעוצבת הבזק (אוגדה 99) לצורכי ניוד בתנאי שטח קשים ובאזורים הדורשים יכולות נהיגה מיוחדות.  פעילות מבצעית לוחמי היחידה מתמחים בנהיגה מבצעית על כלל הכלים בצה״ל, בנהיגת לילה חשוכה במזג אוויר משתנה, והגעה ליעדים מרוחקים מחוץ לגבולות המדינה, באופן מדויק עצמאי ומהיר. יחידת הניוד מבצעת פעילויות ומבצעים מיוחדים רבים בשיתוף פעולה עם יחידות מיוחדות בצה"ל בשלל הגזרות וחזיתות הלחימה במדינת ישראל. פרטיהם של מרבית המבצעים ביחידה אסורים לפרסום בעקבות הצורך לשמור על החשאיות המבצעית של היחידה ואזכוריה בכלי התקשורת מצומצמים ביותר.  מבצע שובו אחים בעקבות חטיפת שלושת בני הישיבה ב־2014, הכריז בית הספר על הקפצת חירום. במבצע שנמשך כשלושה שבועות השתתפו בכל שבוע כ־25 לוחמים, קצינים ואנשי קבע מהיחידה. עיקרי המשימות במבצע היו מעצרים חשוכים ומוארים, מתן אספקה לצוותי הסריקות וצוותי חפ"קים ייעודים שהוקמו למח"ט, לסמח"ט ולמג"דים  מבצע צוק איתן ביולי 2014, עם סיום מבצע "שובו אחים" ובעקבות ירי רקטות תלול מסלול מתמשך על יישובי הדרום פתח צה"ל במבצע "שינוי מסלול" אשר בהמשך התפתח למבצע צוק איתן. היחידה השתתפה במבצע במספר משימות: מחפ"קים ופינוי פצועים ועד לניוד כוחות וצוותים ייעודיים וחבירה ליחידות מובחרות אחרות.  במהלך המבצע פונו על ידי היחידה: 15 פצועים על גבי סבל חי"ר, על ידי כוח הפינוי של חטיבה 261. 7 פצועים, מחבל חמאס עצור וכלב של עוקץ על ידי כוח סיור של חטיבה 35. 3 פצועים על ידי כוח סיור של חטיבה 933. במהלך המבצע היחידה ביצעה הכשרות ורענונים בחירום על רכבי סיור, כלי רכב ממוגנים ורכבים מנהלתיים.  לאחר ההצטרפות לחטיבת המרום בשנת 2018, לאחר עבודות מטה – שונתה כפיפות היחידה מהמרכז לאימונים ביבשה למרום (חטיבת המרום) יחד עם יחידות נוספות כגון עוקץ ולוט"ר. במאי 2021 פעלה היחידה במבצע שומר החומות במסגרתו ביצעה כ-98 מבצעים מיוחדים ומעצרים, ועל כך הוענקה ליחידה תעודת הצטיינות ממפקד אוגדת עזה על תפקודה במהלך המבצע. בשנת 2022 זכתה היחידה בפרס הרמטכ"ל ליחידות מצטיינות כהוקרה על פעילותה במבצעים מיוחדים ועל קידום והובלת תחום הניוד בצה״ל. במרץ 2022 פרץ מבצע שובר גלים ביהודה ושומרון. היחידה לקחה חלק נרחב במבצע במשך יותר משנה בשיתוף פעולה עם יחידות מיוחדות אחרות, איתם ביצעה פעילויות מיוחדות ומאות מעצרים חשוכים ומוארים בכל רחבי יהודה ושומרון. במאי 2023 היחידה לקחה חלק במבצע מגן וחץ אשר במסגרתו פעלה היחידה ברצועת עזה באופן נרחב ביחד עם שלל הכוחות שנלחמו באזור  מבצע בית וגן ביולי 2023, השתתפה היחידה במבצע בית וגן במרחב העיר ומחנה הפליטים ג'נין. היחידה נלחמה לצד חטיבת הקומנדו ובמסגרת המבצע הייתה חלק מפעולות התקפיות וסיכול תשתיות טרור.  מלחמת חרבות ברזל מתקפת הפתע במתקפת הפתע על ישראל מרצועת עזה ב-7 באוקטובר 2023 לוחמי היחידה הוזנקו להגן על היישובים ולהילחם במחבלי חמאס. במהלך הקרבות פעלה היחידה בכלל היישובים, וביצעה שלל משימות שבמהלכן סוכלו מחבלים רבים שחדרו לשטח הארץ ופונו מספר רב של אזרחים, פצועים, והרוגים.  הלחימה הקרקעית ברצועת עזה לוחמי היחידה לקחו חלק נרחב בתמרון הקרקעי בעומק רצועת עזה, ובמהלך הלחימה לקחה היחידה חלק בשלל משימות מיוחדות, בפינוי נפגעים, תספוק וניוד לוחמים. ב-17 בדצמבר במהלך התמרון הקרקעי השתתפה היחידה בקרב בצפון רצועת עזה במהלכה נהרג לוחם היחידה רס"ר (מיל') יוסף אבנר דורן.  גיוס ליחידה ומסלול הלוחם המלש"בים המיועדים, עוברים גיבוש ליחידה שאורכו יומיים שבסופו נקבע אם התקבלו, בנוסף גם נפלטי יחידות מובחרות יכולים להתמיין ליחידה. אלו שעוברים את המיון ליחידה ומתקבלים אליה, מתגייסים באחד משלושה מחזורי הגיוס מרץ, אוגוסט ונובמבר, כל מחזור גיוס מכשיר צוות לוחמים אחד בלבד. מסלול הכשרת הלוחם אינטנסיבי ונמשך יותר משנה, אותו מסיימים הלוחמים ברמת רובאי 07. המסלול מתחיל בטירונות חי"ר ואימון מתקדם מקוצר בפלוגה ייעודית של חטיבת המרום לצד לוחמי עוקץ ולוט"ר בבא"ח צנחנים. לאחר מכן הטירונים עולים ליחידה שם הם עוברים טירונות יחידה שכוללת ניווטים, קורס צניחה, קליעה, לוחמת פרט וצוות, לוחמה בשטח בנוי, קרב מגע ותכנים נוספים. בחודשים שלאחר מכן לומדים הלוחמים את יסודות ואלמנטים הניוד המבצעי. אחר כך ישנם סדרות נוספות במסלול הכוללות מכונאות ותפעול תקלות מורכבות בשטח עוין, תוכני פיקוד והדרכה ועוד. לאחר מכן הלוחמים עוברים סדרה בה הם מתמקצעים בנהיגת כביש, נהיגת שטח ולוחמת ניוד אורבנית על מגוון הכלים הממוגנים. בחלק האחרון והמסכם של ההכשרה, הלוחמים עוברים סדרה אחרונה הכוללת בתוכה לוחמה כצוות ניוד אורגני, סדרות מסכמות של פרט וצוות בשלל התכנים השונים שנלמדו, שבוע הפוך ותרגילים מתגלגלים אינטנסיביים בהם מבצעים את כל התוכן בבסיס בהל"ג לבנות שהתגייסו לשרת כלוחמות בחיל הגנת הגבולות.  תפקידים ופעילות בשגרה ובחירום בשגרה להיות כוח זמין למשימות מיוחדות בשלל הגזרות. להוות גוף מקצועי מכשיר ומסמיך בתחום הנהיגה המבצעית. להוות Unit 444 Mobility, (formerly the Operational Mobility School / BLNM) is an elite IDF unit responsible for training and operational activities in the field of mobility. The unit was established in 2005 by the Ground Forces Command, with the aim of creating a body that would serve as a source of knowledge in the field of operational driving and ongoing security, and to train fighters from all battalions and special units of the IDF. The unit operates in routine, in operations and special and classified activities. The unit operates in cooperation with special units and elite units in the IDF. The unit is a source of authorization and knowledge for complex operations. History and Operational Activity Establishment During 1977, facility 5135 operated in Rafah to train divisional reconnaissance drivers. In 1979, following the peace agreement between Israel and Egypt, the facility moved to Tzeelim. In 1980, the "Intelligence and Reconnaissance School" (MUS) was established for training intelligence and reconnaissance units. In 1996, an operational driving department was established in MUS. In 1999, following an accident involving a Peles 500, an operational driving course was conducted for the first time. In 2001, a field intelligence school (BISLMASH) was established; the operational driving unit remained as part of BISLMASH in Tzeelim. In 2004, following an accident in an exercise of Battalion 71, a decision was made by the Ground Forces Command to establish the Operational Mobility School. Implementation of the decision was carried out in 2005, with the establishment of the school. In 2010, after prolonged staff work, the school expanded to its current structure. Over time, the unit's operational designation sharpened and solidified for carrying out special operational mobility missions in routine and emergency, using wheeled vehicles at the front and in depth. As a result of operational capabilities in the field of mobility, the unit is deployed in emergency situations and is subordinate to the Lightning Formation (Division 99) for mobility needs in difficult terrain conditions and in areas requiring special driving capabilities.

Operational Activity The unit's fighters specialize in operational driving of all IDF vehicles, in dark night driving in changing weather, and reaching distant destinations outside the state's borders, in a precise, independent and rapid manner. The mobility unit carries out many special activities and operations in cooperation with special IDF units in all sectors and combat fronts in the State of Israel. Details of most operations in the unit are prohibited from publication due to the need to maintain the unit's operational secrecy, and its mentions in the media are very limited.

Operation Bring Them Back Following the abduction of three yeshiva students in 2014, the school announced an emergency call-up. In the operation, which lasted approximately three weeks, approximately 25 fighters, officers and permanent staff from the unit participated each week. The main tasks in the operation were dark and illuminated arrests, supplying search teams and specially designated command posts established for brigade, battalion and company commanders.

Operation Protective Edge In July 2014, with the conclusion of Operation "Bring Them Back" and following the continuous trajectory rocket fire on southern settlements, the IDF launched Operation "Course Correction," which later developed into Operation Protective Edge. The unit participated in the operation in several missions: from command post security and evacuation of the wounded to mobility of forces and specialized teams and cooperation with other elite units.

During the operation, the unit evacuated: 15 wounded on a reserve paramedic stretcher, by the evacuation force of Brigade 261. 7 wounded, a detained Hamas operative and a dog of Sting by a reconnaissance force of Brigade 35. 3 wounded by a reconnaissance force of Brigade 933. During the operation, the unit conducted emergency training and refresher courses on reconnaissance vehicles, armored vehicles and administrative vehicles.

Following the joining of the Depth Brigade in 2018, after staff work, the unit's subordination was changed from the Ground Forces Training Center to the Depth Brigade (Depth Brigade) along with other units such as Sting and Lotar. In May 2021, the unit operated in Operation Guardian of the Walls, in which it carried out approximately 98 special operations and arrests, for which the unit was awarded a certificate of excellence from the Gaza Division Commander for its performance during the operation. In 2022, the unit won the Chief of Staff Prize for Outstanding Units in recognition of its activity in special operations and for advancing and leading the mobility field in the IDF. In March 2022, Operation Breaking Waves broke out in Judea and Samaria. The unit took extensive part in the operation for over a year in cooperation with other special units, with which it carried out special activities and hundreds of dark and illuminated arrests throughout Judea and Samaria. In May 2023, the unit took part in Operation Shield and Arrow, in which the unit operated extensively in the Gaza Strip together with all the forces fighting in the area.

Operation Homefront and Kindergarten In July 2023, the unit participated in Operation Homefront and Kindergarten in the city and Jenin refugee camp area. The unit fought alongside the Commando Brigade and as part of the operation was part of offensive operations and terror infrastructure disruption.

Operation Iron Swords The Surprise Attack In the surprise attack on Israel from the Gaza Strip on October 7, 2023, the unit's fighters were deployed to defend the settlements and fight Hamas operatives. During the battles, the unit operated in all the settlements and carried out many tasks during which many operatives who infiltrated into Israeli territory were thwarted and many civilians, wounded and dead were evacuated.

In forecasts threatening a hysterical and historic heat wave about to flood all parts of the country, and we're at Danon school, in the heart of Tel Aviv's bustling port, cooking chicken stock and soups—as if it were December outside. Why exactly? I mean, why learn about this at all, rather than why didn't they postpone the lesson—that's what air conditioning is for. Chef Avihai Mizrachi explained to us that stock is actually the foundation for many dishes and techniques in the kitchen, including soups, stews, and sauces. Chicken or meat stock simmers for a relatively long time—a minimum of 3 hours for chicken stock and up to 10 hours for proper beef stock. Vegetable and fish stocks cook for shorter periods. The section "On the Way to Becoming a Chef" with conclusions, tips, and recipes

**Chicken Stock**

Ingredients for 5.5 liters of stock:
• 2 kg chicken bones/wings
• 2 onions
• 2 stalks of celery
• 2 carrots
• 1 leek
• 10 garlic cloves
• 1 large bouquet garni: parsley, thyme, bay leaves
• 1 clove
• 10 white peppercorns
• 6 liters of water

Preparation:
1. Put the chicken in water and bring to a boil. Skim the foam that rises with a slotted spoon.
2. Cut the vegetables: onion into rings, carrot and celery roughly chopped. Pierce the clove into one of the onion pieces so it doesn't "get lost" in the pot.
3. Prepare the bouquet garni (herb bundle): arrange bay leaves, parsley stems and thyme inside a leek leaf.
4. When the chicken has produced enough foam, add the vegetables, garlic cloves and herb bundle.
5. Simmer for 3 hours and strain the contents.

**Coconut, Galangal and Chicken Soup (Tom Ka Gai)**

Ingredients for 3 servings:
• 250 grams chicken stock
• 70 grams boneless chicken breast cut into strips
• 200 grams coconut milk
• 2 kaffir lime leaves
• 1 shallot, finely minced
• 1 stalk lemongrass, finely minced
• 1 slice galangal (or ginger if unavailable)
• Half a red chili, finely minced
• 6 cilantro stems, chopped + leaves for serving
• 2 tablespoons fish sauce
• 1 tablespoon palm sugar
• 1 lime/lemon juice
• 80 grams oyster mushrooms torn/roughly chopped
• 5 cherry tomatoes, halved

Preparation:
1. Bring the chicken stock to a boil in a pot with the shallot, galangal, lemongrass, cilantro and chili.
2. After boiling, add the sugar, coconut milk and fish sauce.
3. Add the mushrooms and tomatoes and bring back to a boil.
4. Add lime juice and taste to adjust seasoning.
5. Just before serving, add the chicken strips and simmer for about two minutes until cooked through.
6. Serve with cilantro leaves on top with a green salad with herb vinaigrette.

**Green Salad with Herb Vinaigrette**

Ingredients for 6 servings:
• 600 grams mixed greens (recommended: romaine, iceberg, arugula, endive, mâche)
• 50 grams hard cheese with strong flavor (Parmesan, blue cheese)
• 2 pears, thinly sliced
• 4 tablespoons toasted pecan nuts

For the dressing:
• 2 shallots
• 4 tablespoons lemon juice
• 4 tablespoons cherry vinegar (or wine vinegar)
• 2 tablespoons honey
• 1 teaspoon thyme leaves
• 1 teaspoon tarragon leaves (not essential)
• 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard
• 8 tablespoons olive oil
• 8 tablespoons neutral oil
• Salt and white pepper

Preparation:
1. It's best to prepare the salad as close to serving as possible.
2. The dressing: put all ingredients except the oil in a container and blend with an immersion blender. Add the oil and continue blending until you get a uniform emulsion.
3. Tear the greens into large pieces or tear by hand and place in an ice bath. You can add a splash of vinegar to the water. Wash them very thoroughly and wait for the sand to settle to the bottom of the bowl.
4. Remove the greens from the top (don't pour with all the water so they don't mix with the dirt again), into a salad spinner and after drying, place on a plate with paper towels.
5. Serving: put the completely dry greens in a bowl with the pears, nuts and cheese. Pour the dressing over just at serving time and mix by hand. Taste and adjust seasoning. Divide into small plates and serve in a central bowl.

**Five Tips for Vinaigrette:**

Vinaigrette is a classic dressing whose base is an emulsion (suspension) between oil and vinegar, together with seasonings like salt, pepper, mustard, sugar or herbs.

• It's good to use neutral vegetable oil and a bit of olive oil rather than just olive oil, which has a relatively strong flavor.
• In large quantities, or if making vinaigrette with herbs, it's recommended to use an immersion blender. Otherwise, a whisk will suffice.
• Mix the vinegar with the seasonings first, then add the oil. There's no need to add the oil slowly—you can add it all at once.
• The secret is balance between oil and vinegar. If the dressing is too tangy, add oil, not sugar.
• You can store the vinaigrette in the refrigerator. If you've added fruit juices or herbs—no more than a day or two. Before serving, mix well again.

Chef Avivi Mazor and the huge stock pot he cooked are another matter. Learning and habit. That same puff pastry will be almost impossible to make the first time, and after a few times it will become a "recipe with ease" and thus also a so-called "investment." For example, I learned about the precise cuts that have been with me for several weeks now since the cutting lesson. At first it's not easy, slows down the preparation time for cooking and especially gets annoying - but time after time it just works out, and it becomes really much more convenient and correct. 

Not what you thought: The salad that is the hardest to prepare in the lesson afterwards (which was more suitable for the heavy heat and in which we learned about salads and dressings for salads), Chef Hagi Lerner told us that the dish that requires a lot of investment and manpower, and therefore many restaurants avoid it completely, is actually a green salad. Yes, yes, a real leaf salad. A fresh and good one will be very hard to find on menus. The chef demonstrated for us how much time and effort it takes to pick leaves, and especially to wash them properly. For many restaurants, this is an unprofitable investment. At home, on the other hand, it is a very worthwhile investment, and the salad you get will be refreshing, crisp, and delicious - especially if you add a tangy vinaigrette and some good cheese (recipe below). You can cut the tension with a chef's knife. The chef tastes my salads and back to the stock - if you still decide to make stock at home, it turns out that you should not add salt at any stage (due to the reduction of liquids). The stock can be frozen in small boxes, and thus it can be used in the future and upgrade any dish with deep flavor. It is worth making a classic stock with basic flavors, so that it will indeed suit different types of dishes. And most importantly, do not make compromises during cooking, and do not turn the stock into a liquid to which you add everything that is a shame to throw away. 

We also learned that the cutting shape does not have to be precise but it is important to peel and clean the vegetables, and to keep the size more or less the same in the cutting, so that they cook evenly. We made a chicken stock in the lesson and used it for a Thai soup with chicken and coconut milk - Tom Ka Gai. It is a soup that can be a whole meal. The Thai ingredients in it are very important for the flavor and success of the dish, but the stock is no less, and you should not give it up. What's there? Invest a little (: Chicken stock ingredients for 5.5 liters of stock: • 2 kg chicken bones/wings • 2 onions • 2 stalks of American celery • 2 carrots • 1 leek • 10 garlic cloves • 1 large bouquet garni: parsley, thyme, bay leaves • 1 clove of garlic • 10 white peppercorns • 6 liters of water

Method of preparation: 1. Put the chicken in the water and boil. Skim off the foam that rises with a slotted spoon. 2. Cut the vegetables: onions into rings, carrots and celery coarsely. Stick the clove of garlic in one of the onion pieces that will not "get lost" in the pot. 3. Prepare bouquet garni (bundle of herbs): inside a leek leaf arrange bay leaves, parsley and thyme stems. 4. When the chicken has enough foam, add the vegetables, garlic cloves and herb bundle. 5. Cook for 3 hours and strain the contents. 

Coconut, galangal and chicken soup (Tom Ka Gai) ingredients for 3 servings: • 250 g chicken stock • 70 g clean chicken breast cut into strips • 200 g coconut milk • 2 kaffir lime leaves • 1 finely sliced shallot • 1 finely sliced lemongrass stalk • 1 slice of galangal (if not available, ginger) • half a finely sliced red chili • 6 chopped coriander stalks + leaves for serving • 2 tablespoons fish sauce • 1 tablespoon dark sugar • 1 lime/lemon juice • 80 g shredded/roughly chopped Jordan mushrooms • 5 halved cherry tomatoes

Method of preparation: 1. Boil the chicken stock with the shallot, galangal, lemongrass, coriander and chili in a pot. 2. After boiling, add the sugar, coconut milk and fish sauce. 3. Add the mushrooms and tomatoes and boil again. 4. Add lime and taste for seasoning. 5. Just before serving, add the chicken strips and cook for about two minutes until it is ready. 6. Serve with coriander leaves on top of a green salad with herb vinaigrette.

Ingredients for 6 servings: • 600 g mixed leaves (recommended: Arab lettuce, iceberg, arugula, endive, salsify) • 50 g strong-flavored hard cheese (Parmesan, blue cheese) • 2 thinly sliced pears • 4 tablespoons roasted pecans

For the dressing: • 2 shallot onions • 4 tablespoons lemon juice • 4 tablespoons sherry vinegar (or wine vinegar) • 2 tablespoons honey • 1 teaspoon thyme leaves • 1 teaspoon tarragon leaves (optional) • 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard • 8 tablespoons olive oil • 8 tablespoons neutral oil • salt and white pepper

Method of preparation: 1. It is recommended to prepare the salad as close to serving as possible. 2. For the dressing: put all the ingredients except the oil in a blender jar. Add the oil and continue blending until a smooth emulsion is obtained. 3. Cut the leaves coarsely or tear them by hand and place in a cold water bath. You can add a drop of vinegar to the water. Wash them thoroughly and wait for the grit to settle to the bottom of the bowl. 4. Remove the leaves from the top (do not pour out all the water so as not to mix it again with the dirt), do not use a salad spinner and after drying, place on a paper towel tray. 5. Serving: put the completely dry leaves in a bowl with the pears, nuts and cheese. Pour the dressing over just before serving and mix with your hands. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve in small plates in a central bowl. 

Five tips for vinaigrette: Vinaigrette is a classic sauce based on an emulsion (emulsion) between oil and vinegar, along with spices such as salt, pepper, mustard, sugar or herbs. • It is worth using neutral vegetable oil, and a little olive oil and not just olive oil which has a relatively strong taste. • In a relatively large quantity, or if making vinaigrette with herbs, it is recommended to use a blender jar. Otherwise, a whisk will suffice. • First mix the vinegar with the spices and then add the oil. The oil does not need to be added slowly, you can add it all at once. • The secret is balancing the oil and vinegar. If the dressing is too sour, add oil instead of sugar. • The vinaigrette can be kept refrigerated. If you have added fruit juices or herbs – no more than a day or two. Before serving, mix well again. # Carmiel

The Beit HaKerem Valley (Segur Valley), from a topographical perspective, forms the boundary between Upper Galilee and Lower Galilee. The city is built mostly on hills south of the valley and on Mount Carmi in the Segur ridge. The Beit HaKerem Valley together with the Segur ridge, the Sakhnin Valley, and the Jurate ridge form topographically the central Lower Galilee, called the Heart of Galilee. The city of Carmiel is the largest and most central city in this region.

The city was established in the Beit HaKerem Valley (Segur Valley) in 1964, on land partly taken from nearby villages – Deir al-Asad, Majd al-Krum, Baina, and Nahaf. On October 29, 1964, a dedication ceremony was held for the city, in the presence of Prime Minister Levi Eshkol. The establishment of the city was actually part of the So"s plan, which aimed to expand Jewish settlement in central Galilee. The plan was formulated by Levi Eshkol, Yosef Weitz, and his son Re'anan Weitz, with Adam Tal, an aide to Minister Pinchas Sapir, heading the establishment team. The city's location was chosen with the intention of creating a Jewish settlement connection near the Acre-Safed highway, the main road connecting the center of the country with Upper Galilee settlements and the Galilee Finger. In 1969, preparation of the city's master plan was completed, specifying the layout of future infrastructure (road network, water, electrical grid, landscape planning, etc.) for the city. With its expansion, it also occupies land confiscated in 1976, a confiscation that led to the events of Land Day. In 1972, the city received the status of a development town. This status gave the city the ability to attract many young couples due to economic incentives provided by the government. In 1986, Carmiel officially became a city. In the 1990s, over 17,000 immigrants from the former Soviet Union were absorbed into the city, and Israeli-born residents also moved there. Following the withdrawal from South Lebanon in 2000, several families of South Lebanon Army members were absorbed into the city, most of whom settled in the Ramat Rabin neighborhood. During the Second Lebanon War, dozens of Katyusha rockets fell throughout the city, some causing property damage and causing panic. Many families left the city until the end of the war.

In the early 2000s, ultra-Orthodox residents began settling in Carmiel, and ultra-Orthodox educational institutions were established there. In 2000, several dozen families of South Lebanon Army veterans settled in the city, and in the decades that followed, Arab residents and those living throughout the city joined. There is no Arabic-language education system in Carmiel. ## Culture and Tourism

At the entrance to the city, a sculpture park called "Monument to Recovery" was established, featuring works by Jewish sculptor Nicky Imber (1920–1996). The sculptures are made of concrete covered in bronze and include three groups: the Holocaust group – depicting a person surrounded by barbed wire, beside him a person carrying the body of his dying friend, and beside them a woman holding her dying child and pleading for their lives; the Immigration group – a family immigrating with few belongings, led by a grandfather carrying a Torah scroll; Recovery – a young mother fanning her infant as a symbol of hope for the new generation that will grow up in Israel. Near this site stands a monument to Jewish soldiers commemorating Jewish fighters in the Allied armies who fell in World War II. The sculpture resembles a cannon cart topped with helmets bearing the emblems of the Allied powers.

**Galilee Park** – a park covering approximately 100 dunams established in an abandoned quarry. The quarry was renovated and approximately 27,000 plants and some 3,000 trees were planted. Work was carried out in 1993–1994 and the park was formally inaugurated on Independence Day, May 26, 2004. In the center of the park is a waterfalls site, with several water features flowing down the walls of the abandoned quarry, leading to a pool where water lilies bloom. The park also features an observation deck, an open-air theater, and a grove in memory of residents of the city who fell in Israel's wars. On the park's eastern side, the Carmiel municipal building was erected and inaugurated in 1999.

**Rabin Park** with the archaeological site Khirbat Qab. The site contains remains of a Byzantine farm with a wine press, church, and mosaic floor. During the Mamluk period, the place served as a workshop site, and a kiln from the Crusader period was also found there. The current structure on the site is from the Ottoman period.

The site hosts, among other events, the opening and closing ceremonies of the Carmiel Dance Festival and can hold 25,000 spectators.

**Family Park** – a park established in 2007 near City Hall. The park can accommodate 400 people and features facilities and games suitable for the whole family, such as bowling, a mini-golf course, fitness facilities, and more. In 2019, the park was named after former Carmiel mayor Adi Alder.

Secondary education in the city includes three six-year state secondary schools (grades 7–12): ORT Pesgot (junior and high school, a merger of ORT Migdim and ORT Horowitz schools), ORT Karamim (junior and high school), and HaShachar High School, and one four-year high school (grades 9–12), Adam Society and Nature. A Midrasha (Midrash Mattan), Yeshiva Haseder (Carmiel Yeshiva), and for about five years a Yeshiva Matviata and the Torah nucleus "Orot Carmiel," an Engineering College (ORT Braude Engineering Academy), and several professional training bodies also operate in the city.

Children aged 5–18 from throughout the country are educated in the village, aimed at providing these children with a corrective experience and giving them a sense of home and family through a model closest to the family unit. In 2011, an ultra-Orthodox yeshiva called "Rena shel Torah" opened in the city, following which many families from the ultra-Orthodox sector came to live in the city.

**Urban Kibbutz HaMechinkhim** – The kibbutz of the Dror Israel movement, established in the city in 2007. By the mid-2010s, the kibbutz comprised approximately 30 men and women in their late twenties. Kibbutz members teach in formal and informal frameworks throughout the city and the Galilee region.

In 1978, the Children's Village was inaugurated, initially comprising three clusters of 10 children's houses, with each house accommodating 10 children and a foster family living there with their children. In 1980, one cluster was transferred to the military and currently hosts a conversion program for soldiers whose Judaism is in question. Today, approximately 190 children live in the children's villages. # Protests by Ethiopian Israelis

The protests by Ethiopian Israelis are a series of demonstrations held in Israel by Israeli citizens of Ethiopian descent and later by their descendants. In the first decades, the protests focused on the issue of Ethiopian Jewish immigration and its recognition. Subsequently, the protests were directed against racism and police violence. In April 1974, an action committee for rescuing Ethiopian Jews issued a call to the Israeli government and Jewish organizations in the diaspora to rush to save the Jewish community in Ethiopia, which was suffering from famine and attacks. Accordingly, a protest assembly was held in Tel Aviv on Holocaust and Heroism Remembrance Day. On January 7, 1979, a demonstration took place for Ethiopian Jewish immigration and implementation of the Sudanese route, following a meeting two days earlier between leaders of the Union of Ethiopian Jews in Israel and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin. In December 1981, dozens of Ethiopian-origin Israelis held a protest march from Kibbutz Tzova to the Knesset building demanding the immigration of Ethiopian Jews to Israel. According to Moshe Bar-Yuda, these protests were stopped at the request of Menachem Begin's military secretary, Ephraim Foran, for fear that the protests would disrupt the airlift of Ethiopian Jews from Sudanese deserts. In September 1990, hundreds of Ethiopian-origin Israelis demonstrated outside the Prime Minister's office demanding the immigration of 18,000 Jews concentrated in Addis Ababa and, in the meantime, requesting medical aid given the rising mortality of those waiting to immigrate. The protesters blocked traffic for several hours. Police officers, who sympathized with the protest, refrained from dispersing the demonstrators. Absorption Minister Yitzhak Peretz told the protesters that "Russia's gates were closed for over 70 years – and they are waiting a few months," to which the protesters angrily replied that "they have been waiting 2,500 years." At the end of the demonstration, representatives of the protesters met with the Prime Minister's military secretary, Azriel Nevo. Community activists announced that if there was no improvement in the situation, they would bring thousands to the streets. In August 2013, upon completion of Operation Wings of the Dove, the protest movement "Headquarters of the Struggle for Ethiopian Jewish Immigration" held a demonstration outside the Prime Minister's office protesting the closure of immigration, which included approximately 700 demonstrators. In November 2016, as a protest against the government's freeze on the decision to bring the remaining Ethiopian Jews, the headquarters organized a "March of Freedom" together with several Knesset members throughout Jerusalem, which included approximately 1,500 demonstrators. In March 2018, as a protest against delays in continuing immigration, hundreds of activists of the struggle demonstrated outside the Knesset, with Knesset members participating in the demonstration. On July 29, 2018, thousands demonstrated outside the Prime Minister's office against delays in implementing government decisions regarding immigration from Ethiopia.

In 1973, the Rishon LeZion Ovadia Yosef confirmed previous rabbinical rulings regarding the Jewishness of Beta Israel and supported their immigration. However, similar to the Chief Rabbi Isaac Isaac Halevi Herzog before him, Maran Yosef had to address Herzog's concern that the marriages of Beta Israel were valid while their bill of divorce document did not match the emendations of the Sages, a situation that raised concerns about the existence of mamzerim (illegitimate children) among Beta Israel. Rabbi Herzog resolved this halakhic doubt by adding another doubt on top of it regarding the validity of the conversion process that Beta Israel had customarily performed for those joining them. This halakhic solution made it possible to marry Ethiopian immigrants with the rest of the Jewish public in Israel, but it involved a procedure of stringent conversion, including immersion in a mikveh and drawing of covenantal blood, without a blessing, since the entire procedure was done only due to doubt. The early Ethiopian immigrants, including those from the Tigray region, underwent stringent conversion without protest. As immigration increased from the Begamder region in Operation Moses, a sense of humiliation arose among some immigrants because they were converted without their knowledge and against their will, under the guise of medical vaccination. These feelings were intensified by the exposure of the men's nakedness and the requirement to immerse before an audience that observed purity with excessive stringency compared to what was customary in Israel. As a result, a group of immigrants led by Addisu Masala held prolonged demonstrations outside the Knesset building and outside the office of the Chief Rabbinate in Heichal Shlomo during the months of March-October 1985. These protests were described in the protest song "Black Work" which opens the album "Ehud Banai and the Refugees."

On October 2, 1985, Prime Minister Shimon Peres spoke before the demonstrators and promised to address the conversion crisis. According to Moshe Bar-Yuda's testimony, the demonstrators expected that the Prime Minister's promise would be fulfilled similar to the decisions of the Emperor in Ethiopia, and therefore the breaking of the government promise led to an escalation of protests into a 32-day hunger strike. At that time, Lika Kahnat ha-Danna Takuya immigrated to Israel, who led a moderate line of dialogue with the Chief Rabbinate, reached agreement with them, and called on the demonstrators to return home. A halakhic investigation conducted by Rabbi Shlomo Moshe Amar together with his son, Rabbi Yosef ha-Danna, allowed him to eliminate the concern for mamzerim among Beta Israel, since "there is really no validity to their marriages, for the groom never gave anything to the bride... and nothing of acquisition or marriage is said at all... and from everything I asked about this, I saw nothing that pertained to the matter of marriage, neither in the act of giving nor in speech appropriate to marriage." The efforts of Takuya, Bar-Yuda, and the demonstrators led to the cessation of the drawing of covenantal blood, but a national marriage registrar was appointed to examine the Jewishness of spouses at marriage registration. In July 1989, a demonstration was held outside the Knesset by dozens of Ethiopian-origin Israelis against the Chief Rabbinate and the Ministry of Religion demanding permission for community members to marry without immersion. According to the protesters, hundreds of couples who married according to community customs are not recognized as married by the state. These protests gradually led to de facto removal of the Rabbinate's requirements without the Rabbinate formally changing its demand. A legal opinion by Rabbi Menachem Waldman from 1990 and a halakhic ruling by Chief Rabbi Shlomo Moshe Amar from 2003 eliminated the concern for mamzerim among Beta Israel, since their marriages are anyway not valid according to Jewish law. In 1991, Rabbi Moshe Feinstein ruled that according to Jewish law, the Ethiopian immigrants "are not prohibited regarding mamzerim... for there are many doubts regarding them," though he continued to insist on converting them alongside the obligation to integrate them into the Jewish people.

Beta Israel priests in Israel did not receive official status upon their arrival in Israel, partly due to doubt cast on the Jewishness of the entire Ethiopian Jewish community. In Ethiopia, the priests led the community, instructed the public how to conduct themselves according to Torah law, performed marriages, funerals, divorces, and ritual slaughter. Upon their arrival in Israel, the Rabbinate did not recognize the ceremonies performed by the priests and sought to undermine their status. In autumn 1992, groups of Israeli Ethiopian activists organized a series of demonstrations demanding recognition of the priests as performers of religious ceremonies by the state and also payment for them as community rabbis.

# Italian, Kosher and Delicious: Chianti According to Halacha

Terra di Seta winery, located in the heart of Chianti region in Italy, is a kosher winery despite not being obligated to be one, and it offers a wonderful experience, excellent wines and even a kosher dairy restaurant • Our correspondent visited there and returned with a treasure trove of experiences and recommendations

It wasn't difficult to miss the narrow gravel path leading to the boutique Tuscan winery "Terra di Seta," nestled in the heart of Chianti region. The paved road that took us from the city of Siena had ended several kilometers earlier, but Waze led us onto an unpaved road within the dark forest. Only by luck did we spot the modest sign Agriturismo Terra di Seta - pointing to an even narrower path. Upon arrival, we were warmly greeted by Daniel della Seta, the property owner, whose complex includes, beyond the winery building, his private residence, three stunning and secluded guest accommodations, a swimming pool overlooking the horizon, a kosher dairy restaurant (open during tourist season), a vegetable garden where all vegetables and greens for the menu are grown, natural forest, and of course - more than 150 acres of vineyard (almost entirely Sangiovese) and olive groves. The view from every direction opens the heart - rows upon rows of vineyards in varying shades of green, and cypress trees with upright trunks stretching skyward. Every encounter we have with Tuscany is moving, especially one where you discover a wonderful and kosher winery.

The della Seta family is of deep Roman Jewish roots, and their name hints at their historical occupation - weaving of prayer shawls from silk, which were once common among Rome's Jews. Daniel is a biologist by training and served as a lecturer in the field at the Italian Academy. He came to winemaking and agriculture following his wife. "We decided to purchase the property at the beginning of the millennium and in the first years we sold the grapes to wineries in the area," he tells us while strolling through the vineyards at sunset. "In 2007 we understood that we wanted to make our own wine, we built the new winery, and from the start we made the decision to voluntarily subject ourselves to three regulatory systems - that of the Chianti Classico region, organic regulation and the kosher law system. Since the vineyards were old and tired, we started replanting (uprooting the old vines and replanting the vineyards anew) the entire area, plot by plot, and only in the next harvest, 2022, will we harvest grapes from the last replanted plot."

Which regulatory system is the most challenging? Della Seta: "I'm not sure there's an answer to that question. In every regulatory system there are more complex and less complex aspects, and some even overlap. For example, according to both Jewish halacha and the laws of Chianti Classico, the oldest wine region in Italy, in the first three years of vine planting the fruit cannot be used. The soil here is rocky and difficult to work, so the planting process was complex and expensive, but for that reason it's also good for vines, and their roots struggle to penetrate deep into it and reach the water located beneath the surface even without irrigation, which is forbidden here in Chianti. The winery wall, by the way, we built from the stones we cleared from our vineyards."

For wine production, he enlisted renowned Italian wine consultant Enrico Paternoster, who among other things is responsible for the important wine research institute in the land of apple wine, located in Trentino - Istituto Agrario di San Michele all'Adige (IASMA). Paternoster excels at expressing the regional nuances of Chianti in his wines.

The restaurant kitchen produces only local and seasonal dishes based on local agricultural products. Don't look for rare raw materials or pretentious dishes there - everything is based on traditional rural Tuscan cuisine, but what cuisine! Among other things, a wonderful "pappa al pomodoro" is served there - a thick tomato soup made of tomatoes, bread, olive oil, garlic and basil, various bruschettas, panzanella salad, fresh pasta, local fish and more, alongside the winery's wines of course. So simple - so precise and delicious.

Four out of the five winery wines, by the way, are also available in Israel, so whether you've already started planning your upcoming Italian vacation, or if you're staying in the country for now - you can already start enjoying them here.

**Vino di Seta Rosato, 2020** - The only rosé from the winery, yet it too is made 100% from Sangiovese grapes that did not undergo pressing. Its color, contrary to the fashion decree ruling in Israel, shines and sparkles, with a floral and charming nose, a good body of young red fruit and emphasized minerality in a silky texture with a long finish. A delightful wine (12 euros, available at the winery only).

**Toscana, 2019** - The winery's red entry wine, with almost no wood contact (only two months in previously-used barrels), also made 100% Sangiovese. On the nose, fresh red fruits, a typical Brett touch that adds charm, light-to-medium body and delicate tannins. A beauty of a wine for everyday drinking, at a very reasonable price (50 shekels).

**Chianti Classico, 2019** - Made from 95% Sangiovese grapes with a slight addition of Cabernet Sauvignon. 12 months in barrel, a wine rich in raspberry and sour cherry flavors, alongside spice herbs and black pepper. Great depth of flavors, and also an excellent price (75 shekels).

**Chianti Classico Riserva, 2016** – If I had to choose one wine for a desert island, this bottle would probably be at the top of the list. Made from pure local Sangiovese grape and aged 18 months in French oak barrels. Complex, balanced, spiced, fruity, very rich but not heavy with a long finish. Earthy with a unique Chianti character. Produced only in special vintage years. The excellent score (97 points) that the important London wine magazine "Decanter" gave it is completely understandable. A magnificent wine (120 shekels).

**Assai, Gran Selezione, 2015** - The winery's flagship wine, meaning "very" in free translation. Made from grapes from a single vineyard plot that underwent prolonged aging of 24 months in oak barrels and at least another year in the bottle, before its release. Its color is very dark and opaque, with an intense aroma of deep black fruit (blueberries) and flowers. A pleasant body and rich, concentrated texture. A piece of wine (150 shekels).

In the draft Arrangements Law, the Finance Ministry sought to kill two birds with one stone: on one hand, a partial solution to the housing crisis and excess demand for apartments in the real estate market, and on the other hand, addressing the decline in demand for office space, which intensified during the coronavirus crisis. The Finance Ministry addressed giant commercial and employment complexes being built in Israel and existing ones, and sought to convert up to 50% of office buildings to residential apartments. The only problem: opposition from local authority heads, without whom the plan cannot be implemented. The reason for opposition: the property tax rate for commerce and offices is much higher than for residential. Harm alongside benefit

Let us remember that there is harm alongside benefit here. In Britain, the government extended the permit for developers to convert office buildings to residential without the need to comply with building and planning regulations for residential. The British Guardian reported on converting offices to small apartments of 16 square meters, without windows and without minimum living conditions. This situation contradicts our fair rental law, which passed with great difficulty in Israel. The current reality is a celebration for contractors. The Contractors Association is implementing a plan to reduce apartment rents and prices by renovating and converting thousands of offices to residential. The association claims that there are tens of thousands of offices in demand areas that can be converted with renovations of just a month to a residence. Eran Siv, chairman of the Contractors Association: "It is possible and can add tens of thousands of housing units in a very short time. I am confident that this program will significantly reduce rents for young couples and students, and could add tens of thousands more quality housing units."

According to Planning Administration data, Israel has an excess of building rights for offices and employment that are not realized to the extent of approximately 260 million square meters—this is an unfathomable excess that will never be realized in Israel, and in contrast has the potential to build almost all the housing units needed in the coming years. Even the Minister of Construction and Housing and the Minister of Interior themselves addressed the housing crisis and rising apartment prices on several occasions.

A bypass route around bureaucracy

Haim Peigelan, vice president of the Contractors Association of Israel: "As we warned in the Contractors Association long ago, and as all indices have recently shown, the sharp rise in apartment prices, alongside stagnation and declines in office prices, require understanding the market map, which rejects offices and craves residential. According to Peigelan, a critical condition for the law's existence is a process as simple as possible, without dependence on additional planning procedures or exemptions. "We must anchor the developer's right to submit a building permit request to convert office rights to 50% residential without any additional procedure," he emphasizes. If a local authority decides a specific project is worthwhile to convert to residential, the process will advance. Otherwise, it's a plan that will remain on paper."

Former head of the Land Valuers Association Ohad Danos adds: "It's not practical or efficient. You can't take an office building and convert it to residential except with enormous investments, payment of betterment levy and allocation of space in the building for public functions. Danos adds that as far as land is concerned, the situation becomes even more complicated. "Zoning changes would be required, and it usually involves a new plan that would take years. Some companies are adopting a hybrid work model, and estimates are that the new situation will create large surplus office supply in the office market, which some will say was already saturated before coronavirus. Israel is short about 190,000 apartments, and as demographic growth continues the shortage will worsen."

Dalia Assis, land surveyor, city planner and real estate lecturer at Bar Ilan University: "The critical shortage of residential apartments in the demand area and the significant surplus of employment space, offices and commerce necessitate this decision. The dichotomy created over the years between residential areas and employment areas is problematic for two reasons: long commutes burden workers and cause great waste for the economy, and employment zones become desolate in the evenings."

She notes that for the move to succeed, it must be promoted in maximum coordination with local authorities. "We must examine properly the housing needs everywhere, and not create a schematic model of one-third residential and two-thirds employment, which isn't necessarily good for every place."

Architect Gil Shnhav, chairman of CTBUH—the International Council of Tall Buildings in Israel: "In the world, mixed-use has been known for many years. In one building, retail, offices, residential, hotels, culture, leisure and entertainment are combined. When you build a tower of 120 to 160 floors costing about 2 billion dollars, you can't risk occupancy decline. Implementing options for every needed use allows the tower to breathe. If in a certain year there's more need for residential, you add floors at the expense of offices. If you need more hotels, you add floors at the expense of residential. During coronavirus we learned to function under extreme uncertainty. Who survives is not the strongest, but the most flexible. We need buildings that provide adequate solutions for changing needs."

# G-Force Explained

The 'g-force' on a body is its acceleration relative to free fall. We use the term 'force' in this context because such accelerations are not created by gravity itself, but result from other types of forces that cause pressure and tension on bodies. G-force is not directly related to Earth's gravitational force. Generally, in engineering applications, gravitational acceleration g can also help define a unit of measurement for force. As we know, weight is the gravitational force acting on a body and its magnitude is the body's mass multiplied by gravitational acceleration (mg). Therefore, g-force can be thought of as a unit of force measurement, defined such that a body's weight equals a force of 1g. If we say, for example, that 2 g-forces are acting, we actually mean the force intensity is the body's mass times 2g, that is, 2mg. Measurement of 'g-forces' is done using an accelerometer. As mentioned, the term 'g-force' is a misnomer. It is actually the acceleration a mass experiences in a particular situation. On Earth, 1g is approximately 9.8 meters per second squared. For our purposes, let's assume the value is 10 meters per second squared. If we are at 2g, we are actually accelerating at approximately 20 meters per second squared. Most people begin to feel dizzy and even blurred vision due to oxygen deprivation reaching the brain at 4g. This is why amusement park rides (like roller coasters for example) remain within this range of acceleration.

The force acting on a pilot or a person on a roller coaster consists of two components: Earth's gravitational force, which always points toward the center of the Earth, and an additional force resulting from the acceleration of the vehicle itself. The second force is actually a fictitious force because it does not result from pushing or the action of another body.

G-forces acting on pilots:

A pilot in a plane accelerating upward at an acceleration of 5g will feel 5 g-forces downward as a result of the acceleration plus one additional g-force due to his weight, meaning a total of 6 g-forces. The pilot will be pushed forcefully toward the seat and will actually feel the pressure the seat exerts back on him. The pilot will feel 6 times heavier than normal and will even have difficulty raising his arms. In this situation there is a physiological danger because the force acts on the blood downward, preventing blood flow to the brain, which is why the pilot can lose consciousness. Many plants have a dialogue with the animals that eat them, not in spoken language but in shapes and colors designed to catch the eye and stimulate our hunger. To understand how plants speak to us, it's first important to understand what they gain from the deal. When an animal eats a fruit, it takes the fruit's seeds for a ride and "leaves" them somewhere else inside a pile of manure—an excellent starting point for a new plant to sprout. ## How Do Fruits Ripen?

Most fruits ripen in response to the plant hormone ethylene. This is a small molecule carried through the air, which is why to speed up the ripening of avocados or bananas, you should put them in a bag with another ripe fruit. Apples are usually picked before they're ripe and stored in a cooled environment with a high percentage of air filtration and carbon dioxide to prevent them from absorbing the ethylene they themselves emit. This way, you can extend their shelf life by months. Sometimes you see an apple that looks as though only half of it has ripened, and in most cases the reason will be partial exposure to ethylene during the ripening process. Not all plants allow you to do this trick, though—wild berries, for example, must ripen on the branch, and if you pick them too early, they'll rot without ripening.

# Survivor: Everyone Against Everyone

The public auction arrived just in time to show us that from now on it's every survivor for themselves • Coming soon: our bets on the finale • Episodes 44-45 on Matcha

Friends, we're excited to announce - the finale is around the corner. Of course, by "around the corner" we mean you still need to travel dozens more hours through an endless stream of mind-numbing events, take a turn at the "Villa of the Eliminated," stop at "Big Disputes Square," and get stuck at dozens of special traffic lights on the way to the finale. In short, despite there already being an estimated date, there's still a long way to go, and during which, judging by the promo, the survivors will manage to switch alliances like socks. We're in any case starting to bet on who makes it to the finale, but we'll save that for a separate column, if you don't mind.

## A New Era

In Tuesday's episode, the survivors are also starting to smell the finale - Assi is displaying an outward demeanor of calm, but internally he's already divvying up the jury votes. It's not good for him to reach the finale with his allies, since they're actually the ones who could vote for him as jurors, while continuing his competition with them will be a struggle for jury votes already eliminated. They ate from the same trough and that's it.

Assi made a clever and rather surprising move and turned to form an alliance with Eden. The fact that he initiated it perhaps makes him more "dirty," but it's a strategically brilliant move and Eden the tycoon understands this too and was happy to cooperate. This is double risk, because beyond the fact that they need to eliminate their friends delicately so the jurors don't turn against them, they're now dependent on each other's mercy. Assi didn't hesitate to betray his friends in the past, and Eden might still surprise.

In the negotiation hut, Alina befriends herself with her feelings, and gives us another gaping mouth, discovering that she needs to eat a huge bowl of peanut butter to beat Ragev. On the agenda - a conversation with Rafael Chavibi (father of), who understands that Alina's staying will help Eden more and decides to encourage her specifically. Ragev also doesn't seem eager to win the challenge, and Alina scores a first and significant victory.

## Survivor: Island Wretches

## Survivor: What If?

But does the alliance situation get shaken up again like a sponge? Because here Jordan turns to Assi and offers him... wait, what did she offer him? It was something like "I won't leave my alliance and you won't leave yours, but I enjoy watching you play and maybe we'll do something." We didn't understand - do you want to exercise together? Sign up for a macramé class? Join "Bozglos"? Bottom line, Jordan wanted to go and feel free, and Assi gently waved her off, just like a Tinder chat where it's clear it's going nowhere and the other side says "we'll talk tomorrow," really meaning "let's pretend this never happened."

Let's jump ahead to the next duel challenge, which Alina entered skipping. Pier - despite barely seeing her five minutes - we missed her. After Ragev gets irritated for a moment over the word "twisted" ("Why twisted? What did I twist?"), Alina decides to continue their riveting romance and takes him on another challenge. Against the backdrop of a recently published interview with past survivor Omer Rozen, who spoke about how the production wanted competitors' praise, received immunity challenges that seem tailored to their measurements, it's hard not to wonder if this challenge too is at least comfortable for Alina, the dancer with strong stability. Unsurprisingly, she wins and takes Ragev's vote, causing a flip in votes and now Eden and Jordan's alliance is leading.

## Eating the Cake and Keeping It Whole

Saturday's episode opens with Ella's sad confession about struggling to form meaningful connections with girls throughout her life, and we promise if she didn't get a nasty sentence toward someone in the coming episodes, we might start liking her. But never mind - the main course in this episode is the public auction challenge, which is always fun to watch.

A moment before - the social ranking that's not really relevant to anyone except the one ranked last. In this case it's as expected Beni, who was denied participation. Pier, there's nothing worse than that.

We won't mention all the packages, but here are some moments we especially loved:

**The nicest moment:** The "player card" that Eden Chavibi bought, allowing him to either bring Beni into the game or get extra money for himself. Eden of course chooses the friendly/smart strategic move to include Beni in the game. While Israel was quick to bite at the fact that it's all strategy in the food chain, and that Eden doesn't really love Beni, hey - immediately after that karma gave Eden a slap. There's justice in the world.

**The funniest moment:** In this case it's every single one of Ragev's purchases, where Gia kept giving him the chance to swap the package he chose for another, and he kept staying with his choices, until the moment when the weak one lifted and he discovered "essential" items like Botox injections and dental floss. And we thought Beni was the comic character of the season.

**The most-actually-funniest moment:** But with all due respect to Ragev's blunders, Ella fell big into Gia's trap when he announced a package that makes him do rotational movements. And this after she won the useful "makeup-hair" package, right? קרן אור מתקדמת יותר עם יכולות ועוצמות גבוהות יותר מ־IPL, הנותנת מענה של תצורת פולס אינדיבידואלית ללקוח הספציפי. שיטה זו מגיעה לשכבות עמוקות יותר של העור מ־IPL ומתאימה למרבית גוני העור וסוגי השיער השונים. שני סוגי המכשירים מכילים מערכת קירור מובנית בתוך המכשיר, המפחיתה באופן משמעותי תחושת כאב ואי־נעימות. חשוב להבין כי לא כל מכשיר הפועל בשיטת IPL ייתן אותה תוצאה עבור הלקוח, טיב התוצאות משתנה מאדם לאדם. שתי הטכנולוגיות הנפוצות והמקובלות להסרת שיער מבוססות על קרן אור, וההבדל ביניהן בא לידי ביטוי בשני פרמטרים מרכזיים. הראשון הוא צורת הקרן: קרן הלייזר יורדת באורך גל יחיד (ללא פיזור) או מפזרת את קרן האור בצורת פעמון המכסה שטח גדול עם אורכי גל שונים. הפרמטר השני הוא עומק חדירת הקרן - עומק ההגעה של הקרן לתוך שכבת העור. החדירה נמדדת בננומטרים ובהתאמה לכל מכשיר ומטופל, המבצעים מגדירים מהו עומק החדירה שלהם. שני סוגי ביצוע הסרת השיער הם הפופולריים ביותר. הראשון שבהם הוא Alexandrit - המתאים לבעלי עור בהיר (גוון עור 1 עד 3). קרן האור מגיעה לעומק של 755 ננומטר, והמכשיר עובד עם מערכת קירור צמודה להעור. השני הוא DIODE -
